description: Linear A inscription translations, keyed by inscription id. Each entry gives the composite translation and a word-by-word analysis with readings, glosses and confidence.

dialect_notes.description: Two NWS sub-dialects attested in the libation formula corpus. Suffix variation is NOT free variation—it encodes genuine phonological differences between proto-Canaanite/Hebrew (standard, central/south Crete) and proto-Phoenician (Palaikastro, eastern Crete).
dialect_notes.chronological_significance: If the formula dates to MM III–LM IA (~1700–1500 BCE), this is the earliest attestation of the Canaanite dialect split—400+ years before the Ahiram inscription (Byblos, ~1000 BCE).
dialect_notes.decipherment_implication: Any proposed formula reading must yield valid NWS morphology in BOTH dialects simultaneously. This is a powerful constraint for testing candidates.

IOZa2.translation: I make myself a dwelling—O Diqqitu!—in righteousness. So, behold my gathering in the presence of sacred song. May you be favorable toward us.
IOZa2.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—fullest attestation.

PRESERVATION: Five groups are fully preserved. Positions 3–4 are partly or largely restored: line 1 breaks after JA-SA-SA-RA- on face c and resumes with final -SI on face d; GORILA restores [ME · U-NA-KA-NA] from the parallel formulae (GORILA V, 19). The composite translation includes those editorial restorations and reads *301 as /na/: Kober triplets across 17 formula variants point to the verbal root n-w-y 'to dwell' (Ug. nawû, Heb. nāweh), substitution yields 9 independent NWS readings, and NA outperforms the rival r(V) value 9 to 2.

ANALYSIS: TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU is provisionally read from √r-ṣ-y, with analogical 2fs marking followed by a 1cp object; an n-extension remains the principal alternative. STRUCTURE: (1) invocation, positions 1–3; (2) presentation, positions 4–6, with wannā as the hinge and the gathering placed before sacred song; (3) petition, position 7. Diqqitu is compared with Astour's Diqet, the goat-goddess (Ugaritic dqt, √d-q-q; Astour 1966). Position 3 is translated adverbially as *yaššaram*, 'in righteousness'; a divine-name layer remains a secondary possibility.

FINAL BREAK: I-DA-[ is untranslated. It is not a standalone I: GORILA V, 18–19 reads I-DA-[, and Younger estimates a word of approximately six signs. Line 2 ends in the break on face c; face d line 2 is vacat. A related sequence follows the closing petition at Iouktas on IO Za 11 (]U-TI-NU · I-NA-I-DA-•[).

TLZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Sokar, in righteousness. So behold my gathering, [in the presence of sacred song].
TLZa1.notes: Context: Troullos peak-sanctuary libation formula on stone ladle HM 1545. The first four groups through U-NA-KA-NA-SI are preserved. Only NA-MA and SI-RU survive after the damaged interval; I-PI and final TE are formulaic restorations. O-SU-QA-RE is provisionally parsed as vocative ʾō + Sōkar, with final E as the dead spelling vowel after /r/. Geʿez ʾo- supplies a later structural parallel for the vocative (Leslau 1987, 1), not proof of the Bronze Age form; the Egyptian Sokar identification remains CANDIDATE.

Hapax. Vocative addressee in position two, as Sokar at Troullos and Dikte at Iouktas, before dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida.' √t-r-s 'to shield, protect' (Ar. turs; Lane 302); the shield-bearing Kouretes of Ida, and the Sea People Tursha (Egyptian twršꜣ), named from the same root (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

Preferred as a word-specific orthographic or graphic variant of DU-PU₂-RE, independently attested at PKZa15 and HTZb160. Facchetti (1999, 132) and Davis (2013, 44 n. 46) identify *314 here as a PU₂ variant; Thomas (2020, 8) presents the equation cautiously. Under di Mino's Semitic reading, dubur means 'sanctuary, inner sanctum' (√d-b-r). The equation does not assign PU₂ to every *314 attestation.

Preferred as the diptotic genitive in dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida': compare Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/, 'the walls of Ugarit' (Huehnergard 2012, §IV.B.3, p. 40). The older directive analysis 'toward Ida' remains possible, but Ugaritic writes that suffix with consonantal -h /-ah(a)/, so final A alone does not prove it.

U-NA is provisionally vocalized wannā 'and behold,' or, more naturally here, 'so, behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn and Lipiński's reconstruction *wa-hanna/u; the consonantal Ugaritic spelling does not determine the vowels. KA-NA-SI = kanāsī 'my gathering' (G verbal noun of √k-n-s + 1cs -ī); Aramaic-shaped alternative knāšī; Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a verbal rival.
√š-y-r 'sing': abstract šīrūt in -ūt (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

KOZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Tursa, Shield, in the sanctuary of Ida. So, behold my gathering in the presence of sacred song.
KOZa1.notes: TU-RU-SA occupies the formula's variable invocation slot and is therefore treated as a vocative addressee, not a dedicant. Preferred parse: DU-*314-RE is a word-specific variant of DU-PU₂-RE /dubur/ 'sanctuary' (PKZa15; HTZb160; Facchetti 1999, 132; Davis 2013, 44 n. 46; Thomas 2020, 8). I-DA-A is the diptotic genitive ʾIda, 'of Ida'; cf. Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit' (Huehnergard 2012, §IV.B.3, p. 40). U-NA is provisionally /wannā/, comparing Ugaritic w hn ~ wn and *wa-hanna/u; its exact vowels remain reconstructed. 'Toward Ida' remains an alternative.

PSZa2.translation: E: ‘[…]—May she/you answer—[…]—in righteousness.’ TI: ‘[…]—May you (f.) answer—[…]—in righteousness.’
PSZa2.notes:
The Dictaean table carries the sentence that IO Za 6 writes on Iouktas, in the same three groups: TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU · I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, 'May you answer us, my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink, in righteousness.' Here the middle group is broken at its start and ends -JA-(TI/E), where IO Za 6 has the goddess's name and title.

With *301 = NA, TA-NA-I-*301-(TI/E) is the N-stem of √ʿ-n-y 'answer', the bare form of IO Za 6's verb, without the indicative -u, the 2fs clitic -tī and the object -n(u) 'us'. Read with E, it is tanʿanē, 'may she answer' or 'may you answer': final -e comes from the III-y stem, and TA- leaves the person open. GORILA's TI gives tanaʿʿīnā-tī, di Mino's marked 2fs 'may you (f.) answer'.

JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, yaššaram 'in righteousness', closes the sentence, as at Iouktas, Troullos and Palaikastro. ]-RE-I-KE is broken at its start and stays unread.

words.reading: wannā lū kanasti / winnā lū kanasti
words.note: U-NA /wannā/ 'so, behold' + RU /lū/ 'may' + KA-NA-TI /kanasti/, 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s 'gather' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). KA-NA-TI is indexed separately: the coda /s/ is unwritten before /t/, as Linear B drops syllable-final s before a stop (Ventris & Chadwick 1956, 45; pa-ka-na /phasgana/). Rivals: a feminine collective */kanast/* 'may there be a gathering' (compare later Hebrew kəneset 'assembly', Syriac knuštā); /qānastī/ 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8).
√p-n-m. Expanded analytic spelling exclusive to Palaikastro (-MI-NA for standard -MA).
√š-y-r 'to sing' (Heb šīr, Exod 15:1). GORILA IV 34: SI-RU-[·], a lost third sign, not a truncation; SI-RU-[TE] as in the formula is possible (GORILA: SI-RU-DU not excluded).

Compound: I-NA (hinna 'behold!' presentative, the h unwritten; Hebrew hinnēh, Ugaritic hn; Arabic ʾinna is the later ʾ-form) + JA-PA-QA (3ms yaqtul √p-q-ḥ 'to open eyes,' Isa 42:7—guttural ḥ drops, explaining the 3-sign spelling with no missing radical). Theophanic epiphany closure of the PKZa11 prayer. Alt.: ʾina 'when' (cf. Akk. ina) + √p-q-d 'to visit'—'when he visits.' JA-PA-QA attested independently on PKZa12.

PKZa11.translation: I, Pitrī the priest, make myself a dwelling—O Diktaean of the Sanctuary—in righteousness. So, behold, may you gather! In the presence of song… […] …Behold, he opens (his eyes)!
PKZa11.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—longest liturgical inscription (11 words, 25 signs). Palaikastro dialect.

Complete 11-word liturgical inscription—longest in the corpus. The surface order is opening verb → invoked deity and title → proposed speaker's name and priestly title → adverbial formula element → standard body → lacuna → unique closure. Davis (2013, 42–43) and Thomas (2020, 8–10) independently place PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE in the subject/dedicant slot, though they infer two names rather than a name plus title. Reading the pair as 'Pitrī, the priest' supplies the explicit subject of the first-person opening without an unattested 'first-offering' or an unsupported plural vocative. The lacuna between SI-RU and I-NA-JA-PA-QA separates the formula from a masculine verbal closure whose subject remains unnamed.

words.note: Diplomatic U-NA-RU-KA-[?]-JA-SI. Restore U-NA-RU-KA-[NA]-{JA}-SI and normalize U-NA-RU-KA-NA-SI: six parallel witnesses support KA-NA-SI, while -RU- is independently supported by PK Za 11 and IO Za 16. Braces mark JA as a probable scribal intrusion rather than silently deleting it.
No divider follows DU, and the sequence continues into a lacuna. A-PA-DU resembles Ugaritic /ʿabdu/ ‘servant’ (syllabic ab-du; Huehnergard 2012, 92), but the segmentation is not secure.
An isolated preserved JA between lacunae; it does not establish a relative pronoun or a word boundary.

Complete final group, also attested after I-NA on PK Za 11. Proto-Semitic *paqaḥ- and Hebrew/Aramaic √p-q-ḥ mean ‘open (the eyes).’ The omitted final laryngeal and masculine ya- keep the reading provisional.

PKZa12.translation: I make myself a dwelling—[the Diktaean … sacred song? … in righteousness? …]—and behold, may [there be] my gathering … [he opens (his eyes)?].
PKZa12.notes: Fragmentary libation table. Sides b–d contain substantial losses; restorations are formula-guided and remain bracketed. SI and RA-ME belong to separate damaged groups, plausibly SI-RU-[TE] and [A-SA-SA]-RA-ME. The diplomatic U-NA-RU-KA-[?]-JA-SI is normalized as U-NA-RU-KA-[NA]-(JA)-SI: the paradigm predicts KA-NA-SI, while JA is retained as a probable scribal intrusion. The damaged coda cannot securely yield ‘the servant who is appointed’; only final JA-PA-QA is complete enough for a lexical candidate.

words.note: One group on the tablet (GORILA I 141). Ebla ʔa₅-za-ru₁₂ ʔas(ā)r 'locked house' (GlOS 1, 46); its bonded staff as the asirū of the Alalakh VII grain lists (Niedorf 2008, 80 n. 305). Rivals: ʾasīr- 'captives' (Ug. åsr, DULAT 111; Akk. asīru, CAD A/2 331–32); A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen' (aššum, Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399).
*307-PU₂-RE (PK Za 8) = DU-PU₂-RE (PK Za 15).

Its position in the five-entry sum and its distribution in other personnel lists establish a personnel category. An acrophonic DABBĀḤŪ 'sacrificers' reading is circular and has no phonetic complement here. Uchitel 2006, 75 instead proposes an age group.
SigLA analyzes the written unit as one composite sign, A542. Its components cannot be assumed to supply phonetic /lu...qe/. It is therefore not read LUQḤU 'receipts/offerings' on HT89.
'Water' (DULAT 529); under *307 dubur, the sanctuary's water-drawers (Josh 9:27). Rival: Uchitel 2006, 75, Anatolian 'grown-ups'; Finkelberg 1990/91: 80 n. 86 gives only the Luwian -mi ending.
VIR secures the human referent; *313a supplies an unknown qualification. RĀQIḪŪ 'perfumers' remains an unsupported contextual conjecture because the sign has no phonetic complement.
Ug. ṯġr 'gatekeeper', a personnel class (DULAT 888); gatekeepers of the house of God, Ezra 7:24. Rival: Akkadian tārû 'child-minder'.
23+22+24+13+5 = 87. Arithmetic establishes the summation function independently. Semitic *kull- 'all, entirety' is a possible etymological comparison; Linear B normally uses TO-SO for 'total.'
Cyperus, not cypress or copper. This begins the separate post-total commodity section. The value ¾ for A732 follows a modern fraction model and is not universally agreed.
AB30 functions logographically as FIC; NI is its syllabic value. The value ¼ for A704 is a defensible modern interpretation rather than an uncontested reading.
AB131a is the wine logogram; the final numeral is damaged.

HT89.translation: The work-house of the sanctuary. Personnel classes: *305 23; A542 22; water(-men) 24; VIR+*313a 13; gatekeepers 5—total 87. Cyperus 2 + fraction; figs 2 + fraction; wine 6(?).
HT89.notes: HT89 is a personnel list followed by a separate commodity section. A-SA-RA₂ is one group on the tablet: /ʾasāra/ 'locked house, work-house', with the vowels of Ebla ʔa₅-za-ru₁₂ (GlOS 1, 46), CANDIDATE; rivals /ʾasīr-/ 'captives' (Ug. åsr, DULAT 111; Akk. asīru, CAD A/2 331–32) and A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen'. Uchitel includes *305, A542, MA-I-MI, VIR+*313a, and TA-RA among qualifications of personnel. Their counts sum exactly: 23+22+24+13+5 = KU-RO 87. Only after that total do A303/CYP, AB30/FIC, and AB131a/VIN appear. *307 is dubur 'sanctuary' (PK Za 8 = PK Za 15); MA-I-MI 'water(-men)' and TA-RA 'gatekeepers' are SPECULATIVE. The expansions 'sacrificers,' 'offerings,' 'perfumers,' and 'turtledoves' are not established. Fraction values ¾ and ¼ are model-dependent, and the final wine numeral is damaged.

words.gloss: final preserved sign of a lost word; not a standalone AROM logogram in this context
completion of yaššaram across a word-internal line break
and behold, may [...]; comparison with related formulae permits, but does not restore, a gathering clause

IOZa16.notes: Fragmentary libation table from the Iouktas peak sanctuary, MM III B–LM I. Diplomatic text: ] *123 · JA-SA-SA-RA- / -ME · U-NA-RU-KA[. The opening *123 is the final sign of a lost word; Karetsou, Godart, and Olivier (2002–2003, 445 n. 26) reject a standalone logographic reading in this context. The line break within JA-SA-SA-RA-ME is not a divider. At the other edge, only U-NA-RU-KA is preserved. Comparison with PK Za 11 and the U-NA-(RU)-KA-NA-SI/TI family permits a gathering clause as a bracketed reconstruction, but the editors explicitly decline to choose the lost ending (pp. 446–47). RU may represent Akkadian-style lū introducing a positive injunction in a verbless clause (Huehnergard 1997 §22.2), but its value remains uncertain (Duhoux 1992, 69–70; Thomas 2020, 2–3).

words.note: The inscription begins at a broken edge before NU. NU may be an asseverative particle (cf. Ug. n, Heb. nā, Akk. nū), but it may instead complete a lost word; it cannot be translated independently with confidence.

Possible b-preposition (cf. Heb. bə-, Ug. b-, Amarna bi-). A divider follows PA₃-E, while the Semitic preposition is normally proclitic, and the next group is presently read as a vocative. Its complement and exact syntax remain unresolved.

Name + nisbe -TE-TE + *307-PU₂-RE dubur, the logogram with phonetic complement. TE-TE is the feminine nisbe -īt, Diqqitīt "the Diktaean" (see A-DI-KI-TE-TE), one sign group with dubur in each witness (PKZa8, PKZa11, PKZa15): Diqqitīt dubur "the Diktaean of the sanctuary".

Normalized TU-ME-I follows GORILA/Valério; Younger regards only TU as secure and questions whether the remaining traces form this group. ME is partial and I survives as three prong tops at the broken corner (GORILA IV 25). PK Za 14 ]-TU-ME-I · JA-SA-SA-[ secures the end of the group. If correct, Hebrew תֻּמִּי tummī 'my wholeness/integrity' (Ps 7:9; 26:1) supplies the exact nominal shape. 'Wholeness' preserves √t-m-m 'complete, without defect' while distinguishing it from the following √y-š-r 'uprightness/righteousness.' The imperative alternative 'be made whole!' is secondary.

Only JA-SA survives before a lacuna. Valério restores JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] from the recurrent libation-formula word and prints a word divider before U-NA-KA-NA-SI; Younger's transcription likewise separates the two across the lacuna. The restored signs are not preserved, but the passage is two groups, not one word JA-SA-U-NA-KA-NA-SI.

Preserved after the lacuna following JA-SA. The semantic segmentation U-NA | KA-NA-SI is morphological, not marked by a written divider: conjunction + contracted presentative + 'my gathering.' The sequence is damaged again after SI.
Only I-PI survives at the broken end. Formulaic position supports restoration toward I-PI-[NA-MA] 'in the presence of,' but PKZa8 does not attest a complete standalone I-PI or the lost continuation.

PKZa8.translation: […] In/at […]—O Diktaean of the Sanctuary—my wholeness, [in righteousness]. So, behold my gathering in the pres[ence of …]
PKZa8.notes: Context: Fragmentary Palaikastro libation formula with DUBUR logogram and phonetic complement. Diplomatic sequence: ]NU · PA₃-E · JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE · TU-ME-I / JA-SA[ … ] U-NA-KA-NA-SI[ … ] / I-PI[ … ]. Valério 2007 restores JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] | U-NA-KA-NA-SI, two groups, not one continuous word. JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] and I-PI-[NA-MA] remain formulaic restorations, not preserved text. The translation leaves the opening and closing damage visible. TU-ME-I is rendered 'my wholeness' to distinguish √t-m-m completeness from √y-š-r righteousness while retaining their ritual pairing.

words.gloss: O Diktaean of the Sanctuary (vocative yā + Diqqitīt + dubur)
words.note: Same phrase as PKZa8 with *307. TE-TE is the feminine nisbe -īt, Diqqitīt "the Diktaean" (see A-DI-KI-TE-TE), one sign group with dubur in each witness (PKZa8, PKZa11, PKZa15): Diqqitīt dubur "the Diktaean of the sanctuary".

PKZa15.notes: Libation table rim (A.Nik. M.2469), left to right. GORILA IV 41: ] · JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE [ — a divider before JA, preceded by the trace of a sign (p.-ê. JA); broken after RE. Marked incomplete: text lost on both sides.

words.note: WA runs into the break; JA restored from the ten other witnesses.
Thomas 2020, 20 distinguishes only KA-NA, broken on both sides. Younger reads ]•-•-•SE-KA-NA-SI[•]TE[ and Hogan ∙ ∙ ∙ -ṢẸ-KA-NA-ṢI-[∙] ṬẸ-[, with SE, SI and TE uncertain and no divider. Not readable.
√š-y-r 'sing': abstract šīrūt in -ūt (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

SYZa3.translation: I make myself a dwelling […]-KA-NA-[…] sacred song.
SYZa3.notes: Context: Syme libation formula, fragmentary. Thomas 2020, 20 distinguishes only A-ṬẠ-Ị-*3̣0̣1-WA-[…]-KA-NA-[…] SI-RU-TE, with substantial text lost between the fragments (GORILA V 66–67, before the joins: ca. 20 signs). KA-NA stands in formula position 4, where the other sites have U-NA-KA-NA-SI.

words.gloss: O Šumāt! Olive (vocative + proper name + commodity ideogram)
words.note: Segment JA | SU-MA-TU: JA = Semitic vocative yā, paralleling JA-DI-KI-TU /yā Diktu/ in the same formula position. Birot, as reported by Huffmon (1965, p. 252), suggests that Amorite sumat- is a plural of sum- ‘name (> posterity),’ yielding *šum- + *-āt → Šumāt; TU carries a dead vowel after final /t/, and vowel length is unmarked. The corpus follows GORILA V 64–65 and Davis in reading the following sign as OLIV; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read it as syllabic RE, which may extend the name.

Beside OLE, compare √k-n-s for gathering produce as a cult offering: Neh 12:44 appoints men over the storerooms 'to gather into them' (לִכְנוֹס liḵnôs) the contributions, first fruits and tithes for the priests and Levites.

words.gloss: possible divine name or liturgical predicate; untranslated
words.note: A-JA is complete in GORILA V, 64–65. Mari writes West Semitic ḥaya "lives" as both ha-ia- and a-ia-, and Alalakh VII alternates a-ia-/ha-ia- in the same name; Weeden (2009, 96–100) suggests that a-ia- may reproduce an unrepresented /ḥ/. The Mesopotamian god Haya is independently written dḫa-ià and invoked in the Old Babylonian Hymn to Haia for Rim-Sin (ETCSL 2.6.9.2; line 59 links him with the petition "Give me life!"). Keep Haya, /ḥaya/ or /ḥayyā/ "(the) Living One/Life", and the goddess Aya as separate alternatives.

SYZa2.translation: I make myself a dwelling. O Šumāt! Olive, 1. So, behold my gathering: oil. [Haya?/the Living One?/Aya?]
SYZa2.notes: Context: Syme dialect libation formula with OLIV and OLE commodity ideograms. The sign immediately after SU-MA-TU is epigraphically disputed: GORILA V 64–65 and Davis read OLIV; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read RE. Final A-JA is complete, but its interpretation remains open: Haya, a √ḥ-y-y predicate or epithet, Aya, and Davis's "much" are rivals.

words.note: Not readable.

PKZa20.notes: Only U-NA-KA-[ survives, broken after KA; the word ran on, perhaps to U-NA-KA-NA-SI.

words.note: Predicate before A-NA-NE in undivided JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE, as kî-yāšār dəbar-YHWH 'for righteous is the word of YHWH' (Ps 33:4).
GORILA IV 125 prints WI-PI-[·], one sign lost after PI. Not readable.

KNZc7.translation: This bowl, a dove—O Athirat, righteous is (thy) grace …
KNZc7.notes:
Context: ritual text painted inside a mended short conical cup; no numerals.

GORILA IV, 125 begins directly with complete A-KA-NU-ZA-TI and marks no opening lacuna, so there is no positive evidence for a lost word before A-KA-NU. Gordon segments that continuous group as A-KA-NU | ZA-TI. ZA-TI may be /zāt/ 'this' (historically perhaps /zāʾt/), with TI spelling final /t/ and a nonphonemic support vowel. Hebrew zō(ʾ)t supplies the lexical parallel. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, and FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl' supplies the closest structural parallel (Krahmalkov 2000, 31). Its postposed Semitic order is rendered naturally in English as 'this bowl.' The rival /ḏāti/ 'of' fits less well: its final /i/ is a live genitive ending, and the agreement frame it needs is absent. The segmentation remains CANDIDATE: ZA-TI is a hapax, SigLA reads ZE rather than ZA, and final TI = /t/ is not independently established. DU-RA-RE is durār 'dove', Hebrew dərôr, a bird (HALOT, 230), the offering a votary holds out beside the Knossian Dove Goddess (Evans, PoM II 337, 339); the cups lay above the crypt of the dove vase (PoM I 587). The dove is the Goddess's bird: on the Knossian shrine columns doves are "the outward and visible sign of the divine presence" (Evans, PoM I 222); in Syria the dove is her symbol and her messenger, and the dove goddess appears in Crete, Cyprus and Mycenae from the mid-second millennium (Winter in Keel 1977, 52, 74, 76); doves attend Tanit (Dever 2005, 232). The dərôr is also a bird of purification: the leper is cleansed with two clean birds, one slaughtered into an earthenware vessel over living water (Lev 14:4–7), which the Mishnah names ṣippŏrîm dərôr (m. Negaʿim 14:1); doves are the purification offering after childbirth (Lev 12:6–8), as Ugaritic ynt and tr are offered (Milgrom 1991, 758). A Nabataean inscription from Petra begins [d]nh ʾgnʾ dy qrb, 'This is the basin which ... offered,' and proceeds to the deity and bšlm šlm, 'in peace, peace' (CIS II 423b; Milik 1972, 109; Alpass 2013, 102 no. 16); it supports the vessel–deity–blessing frame but contains an explicit dedication verb. JA-SA-RA | A-NA-NE puts the predicate first, as kî-yāšār dəbar-YHWH 'for righteous is the word of YHWH' (Ps 33:4) and kî-yāšār YHWH (Ps 92:16). The final group is WI-PI-[·] (GORILA IV, 125), one sign lost after PI. Not readable. For the incantation-bowl parallel (Marinatos 1951, 41; Franceschetti 1990, 40–41), see KN Zc 6.

words.note: PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

HT95a.translation: Settlement(s): grain. Blood (ritual category) 10, count/reckoning 10, king/royal establishment 20, emmer 10, nobles/council 10, parched grain 7.
HT95a.notes: Context: Grain allocation—administrative tablet with GRA ideogram and commodity distributions. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a recurring quantified ritual category; rivals dimtu 'district', Aramaic dmy 'value'. KU-NI-SU is kunīšu 'emmer', an Akkadian loan (Nuzi ku-ni-šu, CAD K 537). With QE-RA₂-U /qelwu/ 'parched grain' it is one of two grain products in the set.

words.note: √m-k-r 'to trade': Ugaritic mkrm 'merchants', counted in rosters with a total (DULAT 537); Akkadian mākiru, makkāru 'trader' (CAD M/1 129, 131). TE the -t of a class noun, cf. Akkadian tamkārūtu 'merchants (collective)' (CAD T 141). Rival: makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138).

HT117a.translation: Merchants—owed: Ummī-naśiʾ: ʾUšu 1, Mītu 1, Kurmu ('Vineyard') 1, Maruʾ ('Fattened') 1, Kubānu 1, Tuʿlum 1, ʾUdmī 1, Mīru-darār ('Free-running Bull') 1, Teyar 1, Nadr ('Vow') 1. Total: 10. Šata: Kukkadal 1, Kōšayīt ('the Kushite woman') 1, Ḏā-Mīnu 1, Ḏā-naquddi 1, Qidaru 1.
HT117a.notes:
Context: Personnel list—individual names with qty 1 allocations

MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' heads a roster of men owing 1 each, as Ugaritic lists count mkrm 'merchants' with a total (ġr mkrm, DULAT 537); rival makritu 'red' (CAD M/1 138). One written word in both witnesses. Personnel allocation list with named recipients. KI-RO is 'owed', not 'all, total'. U-MI-NA-SI heads the roster outside the count: the ten one-unit entries from U-SU to NA-DA-RE make KU-RO 10. KI-DA-RO is the personal name Qidaru, last of the SA-TA roster below the ruling. Six of the fifteen names recur as men's names in Linear B at Knossos: U-SU u-su (KN V 7512), TE-JA-RE te-ja-ro (KN V 479), NA-DA-RE no-da-ro (KN As 609), KU-KU-DA-RA ku-ka-da-ro (KN Uf 836), DA-MI-NU da-mi-ni-jo (KN D series), KI-DA-RO ki-da-ro (KN E 842); MA-RU compares with ma-ro at Pylos (PY Cn 328) (DMic I–II). Both sections list persons.

devotee of Kubaba (personal name or title); rival Gupana
personal name; Ugaritic ålnr (Hurrian), Linear B a-ra-na-ro

HT1.translation: Parched grain(?). Outstanding: 197. Zuzu(?) 70; Dīdī-zakī 52; Kubānu 109; Aranare 105.
HT1.notes: Substantially intact LM IB administrative roster; no commodity logogram is present. KI-RO 197 is not a total: the four following quantities sum to 336. QE-RA₂-U /qelwu/ 'parched grain' heads the list, as it closes the HT95a/b grain set. ZU-SU compares with the Late Bronze Age Ugaritic personal name {m}zu-zu (RSO 7, 3, lower edge 3; ORACC P347841), though SU/ZU remains unexplained. DI-DI-ZA-KE has no secure external analysis. KU-PA₃-NU is Kubānu 'devotee of Kubaba', masculine of KU-PA₃-NA-TU Kubānatu (di Mino, Ya Diktu); the rival compares Ugaritic syllabic {m}gu-pa-na (RS 11.839 r.8; ORACC P503288), alphabetic Gupan, and Linear B ku-pa-nu-we-to. A-RA-NA-RE is the Hurrian name Ugaritic ålnr, which DULAT sets beside Linear B a-ra-na-ro (DULAT 57; KN As 1516.11); Gordon's Egyptian 'Great-is-the-name-of-Re' is the rival.

Storm God (= Hadad/Baal, section 2 heading); rival adû 'work assignment'

words.note: PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.
√q-l-w with RA₂=/la/: stands in the slot of QE-RA₂-U qelwu 'parched grain' in the HT95a/b set. Rival: Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' (DULAT 703; disputed as a PN).

HT86a.translation: Section 1—Agaru: emmer, GRA+K+L: 20; king/royal establishment: 20; nobles/council: 20; parched grain: 10. Section 2—Addu: blood (ritual category), GRA+B: 20; count/reckoning: 20.
HT86a.notes: Context: Two-section Haghia Triada allocation ledger, Casa Room 7. The preserved integer entries sum to 110; the GRA+K+L and GRA+B ligatures carry metrological riders and are not securely distinct grain species. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a recurring quantified ritual category; rivals dimtu 'district' and Imperial Aramaic dmy nksyʾ 'the value of the property' (TAD B2.6 R.14), a later comparison. QA-RA₂-WA is read qalwa 'parched grain' (√q-l-w): it closes the HT95a/b set where QE-RA₂-U qelwu stands; rivals Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' and Linear B qa-ra₂-wo, a personal name. KU-NI-SU is kunīšu 'emmer', an Akkadian loan (Nuzi ku-ni-šu, CAD K 537), with the grain sign on its line. HT86b is an erased draft of the opening lines, not an independent witness.

HT86b.translation: [Erased draft of HT86a lines 1–3:] Agaru: emmer, GRA+K+L: 20; king/royal establishment: 20; DI-DE[…].
HT86b.notes: Side b is an erased first text: GORILA I 135 sets every line in erasure brackets, 'texte actuel sur premier palimpseste'. It repeats HT86a lines 1–3 (A-KA-RU · KU-NI-SU GRA+K+L 20, SA-RU 20, DI-DE-RU 20) and is not an independent witness. DI-DE is the start of side a's DI-DE-RU; the erased text ends there.

RE-ZA is (ʾa)raz 'cedar', counted beside cyperus on KH 86; rival Luwian aruza, a measure. KI-KI-NA is Kikkina, as Amorite KI-IK-KI-NI. KU-PA₃-NU is Kubānu 'devotee of Kubaba', beside KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba; rival Gupana. PA-JA-RE is Payare, Egyptian Pꜣ-Rꜥ 'He (of) Re', Linear B pa-ja-ro. in, with, by (proclitic b-); rival bād(i) 'in the charge of'

HT103.translation: ʿŪta: figs 40; by Takušenni ]6½; buṭnu (*188), a Pistacia product, 13; Daguna 1; Takušenni 1; garden 5½.
HT103.notes: Administrative list under U-TA₂ · NI 40, HT Scribe 3. GORILA reads .2–3 PA₃-DA-KU-SE-NE[ ]6½, broken after NE, and allows a divider after PA₃ (GORILA I 171), as Ugaritic often sets one after a one-syllable proclitic, b. bnk (CAT 1.6:I:46; Tropper 2000, §21.412a): bi= 'by, with', the proclitic of PH 6 I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI. Rival: bād(i) 'in the charge of', as Kition no. 84 bd with a personal name and a count of workmen (Krahmalkov 2000, 97) and CAT 4.145:9–10 bd rb ḥršm (Huehnergard 2012, 76, 94); Linear B pa-ro with a personal name is the Aegean parallel (Killen 2024, 103). Weak point: HT 103 wants bd 'in the charge of', and no Semitic text shortens bd to b. NI is the fig: AB 30 draws a fig branch (Montecchi 2024, 178, following Neumann 1957, 157–58); NI 40 is no total, and no KU-RO follows. DA-KU-SE-NE recurs with 1, and on HT 104 as DA-KU-SE-NE-TI; the first writing is damaged in two sign positions in SigLA. DA-KU-NA is Daguna, a name on Dagan (HALOT 213). *188 is buṭnu, the Pistacia product (HALOT 121; CAD B 358). KI-RA kirû 'garden, orchard' (CAD K 411) also heads the fig entry on ZA 8; rival qīru 'hot bitumen' (CAD Q 270).

hapax transaction sign; exact operation unknown
probable Hurrian-style name or entity with final TI: 45½
words.note: Bare DA-KU-SE-NE occurs on HT 103 .4–5; on .2–3 a break follows NE. The comparison with Boğazköy Tagu(b)-šini (Laroche 1980, 250) and Ugaritic Taki-šenni supports the name analysis, but the exact form and the function of TI remain uncertain.
On the Eblaite name element yidu 'strength' (Pagan 1998); TI is the ending of all three names under TA-PA.
No verified Luwian or Semitic match. HT 20 .1 reads PA-RO-SU; with PA-RO here (Schoep 2002, 47) it is that name with the -TI of the two entries above.

HT104.notes: Inter-entity transfer list with an unspecified commodity and unresolved direction. The arithmetic is exact: 45½ + 20½ + 29 = 95. Repeated final TI defines a shared administrative or morphological class. The DA-KU-SE-NE / DA-KU-SE-NE-TI pair favors suffixation, while GORILA I 171 allows TI to be an ideogram or classifier.

words.note: The inscription begins at a broken edge. TA is the preserved end of a word, not an independently attested particle.

widd 'love' + ti(h)āmu 'the Deep' (Ug. thm, DULAT 851; Heb. təhôm), as Ug. ydd il 'beloved of El'. Sign dispute: GORILA IV 161 reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading takes the fourth sign as RU.
Feminine participle of √w-q-d 'to burn', as Heb. yōqedet (Isa 65:5), with w- written by U as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI. A divider separates it from WI-TE-JA-MU (GORILA IV 161).

JA-SA-SA-RA is preserved, followed only by a damaged vertical trace. ME is the conventional formulaic restoration; NE cannot be excluded. The established formulaic lexeme permits the tentative contextual gloss, but PL Zf 1 does not independently preserve its ending.

Proposed internal segmentation TA-NU-NI / KI-NA: expected Hebrew 2fs Piʿel imperative /tannî/ from √t-n-y ‘recount, recite’ (Judg 5:11; 11:40) plus qînâ ‘funeral song, dirge’ (HALOT, 1097, 1759–60). HALOT's proposed antiphonal repetition motivates the natural translation ‘chant a dirge’; the stricter lexical gloss is ‘recite/repeat.’ The funerary context suits the phrase, but the inscription writes no divider between the two proposed words.

Its position after the proposed imperative-object phrase favors a noun, contextually a vocative. Hebrew nîn means ‘offspring, descendants.’ NI-NU-NI can spell /nīn-ūn/ exactly if final I is dead; alternatively /nīn-un/ would contain Arabic-type nominative nunation. Both are grammatically regular Semitic analyses: -ūn may represent plural or collective morphology, while -un is an indefinite nominative ending. What remains uncertain is which ending the Linear A spelling encodes and whether the noun functions as a vocative here. Since this exact inflected form is unattested for nîn and NI-NU-NI is a hapax, the identification remains speculative. CAD N/2 supplies no Akkadian ninû ‘offspring.’
One lost sign flanks I on each side (GORILA IV 161, which allows [·]-I-MA); it is not a standalone word or suffixal attestation.

PLZf1.translation: […] Beloved of the Deep(?), the Burning One(?), in righteousness(?)—Chant a dirge, O offspring. […]
PLZf1.coverage: Every group but the broken ]TA and [?]-I-[?] receives a tentative gloss
PLZf1.notes: PL Zf 1 is a fragmentary LM I inscription on a silver pin from the immediate vicinity of Platanos Tholos A, a funerary rather than peak-sanctuary context (Monti 2022, 113). It is read sinistroverse. Initial ]TA and final [?]-I-[?] are word fragments, WI and MU in WI-TE-JA-MU are doubtful, and the ending of JA-SA-SA-RA-[ME?] is restored. The final preserved phrase is provisionally read /tannî qînâ nīnūn/, ‘Chant a dirge, O offspring.’ The lack of a divider within TA-NU-NI-KI-NA and the ambiguity between grammatically regular plural/collective -ūn and case -un keep the identifications speculative; the morphology itself is well formed. ‘Posterity’ remains a possible interpretive gloss for /nīnūn/, not the direct translation. Duhoux's structural analysis makes WI-TE-JA-MU and U-QE-TI possible onomastic X-terms, but this is a syntactic classification, not a decipherment.

Duhoux 1992, 80–81: supplementary X-terms as possible personal names
Monti 2022, 113: funerary context; not a votive offering

IOZa9.support: Surviving corner of a square marble libation table (HM 3898)

words.note: Proposed adverbial accusative /yaššaram/ from √y-š-r; -am is represented by final ME. On IO Za 9 only ]JA-SA-SA- survives; GORILA restores RA-ME (V 33).

U-NA is provisionally /wannā/ 'and behold,' or, more naturally here, 'so, behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u; the vowels remain reconstructed. KA-NA-SI = kanāsī 'my gathering' (G verbal noun of √k-n-s + 1cs -ī); Aramaic-shaped alternative knāšī; Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a verbal rival. On IO Za 9 only U̇-NA-KA-[ survives; GORILA restores NA-SI (V 33).

IOZa9.notes: IO Za 9 is preserved on the broken corner of a square marble libation table. Line a is retrograde and line b runs in the opposite direction, so both read outward from the corner (GORILA V, 32–33; Younger 2023, citing Palaima 1988, 310–12). Line a keeps ]JA-SA-SA- and line b U̇-NA-KA-[; GORILA and Younger restore RA-ME and NA-SI from the formula. Both words are read in full elsewhere: JA-SA-SA-RA-ME on IO Za 6 and PS Za 2, U-NA-KA-NA-SI on KO Za 1, PK Za 8, SY Za 2 and TL Za 1. PK Za 27 breaks after U-NA-KA- too.

words.note: Preserved after a broken left edge: ]I-PI-NA-MA. The p-n 'face/front' family supports the contextual sense 'in the presence of'; -MA may be an enclitic =ma.

TE is read beyond a damaged join after RU: SI-RU[-TE. The normalized form is secured by intact formulaic parallels. √š-y-r 'sing': possible abstract šīrūt in -ūt; Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'.

IOZa15.translation: […] in the presence of sacred song.
IOZa15.notes: Damaged witness of positions 5–6 of the IO Za 2 formula: ]I-PI-NA-MA · SI-RU[-TE. The preceding text is lost, and TE is read beyond a damaged join after RU. The normalized pair is supported by intact IO Za 2 and KO Za 1. I-PI-NA-MA is interpreted contextually as 'in the presence of'; 'sacred song' renders the proposed abstract šīrūt from √š-y-r, not 'service/ministry' from √š-r-t.

words.note: The complete first group permits the adverbial accusative *yaššaram*, 'in righteousness.'

Only Ụ-NA-KA- is reasonably preserved; the following trace may belong to NA, while final SI is lost. The editors prefer AB10 U over AB45 DE from the outline and formulaic context. Restoration as U-NA-KA-[NA-SI] follows the recurrent formula, so both kanāsī and its 1cs suffix remain restored here.

PKZa27.notes: The Neopalatial Petsophas fragment preserves complete JA-SA-SA-RA-ME after a divider, followed by Ụ-NA-KA-[ or possibly Ụ-NA-KA-ṆẠ[ before the break (Knappett, Del Freo, and Zurbach 2017, 73–80). It belongs to the same abbreviated formulaic pair as IO Za 9 but is not an independently complete duplicate. No preserved element means 'holy.'

words.note: The vessel is broken before TE. This is the end of a lost word, not an independently attested TE particle; [SI-RU]-TE is a possible restoration but is not epigraphically recoverable.

I-DA is the inscription's only complete group: it is bounded by dividers despite the breaks on both outer edges. Mount Ida (Psiloritis), the sacred mountain of central Crete; the name is 'the Hand', PS *yad- ~ *ʾid- (semitic_roots 2046), with the Idaean Daktyls, 'fingers', as the Greek doublet (di Mino, Ya Diktu p. 19 n. 34).

The second JA reaches the broken right edge; no divider or word ending survives. The preserved beginning may continue a form of Semitic √ḥ-y-y 'live; life,' allowing the contextual restoration '[the Living One …],' but JA-JA is not a complete word and cannot independently establish /ḥayyā/.

PKZa18.coverage: 1/1 complete word translated; 2 edge fragments untranslated
PKZa18.notes: Context: broken stone-vessel inscription from Palaikastro. Diplomatic text: ]-TE · I-DA · JA-JA-[…. Both outer groups run into breaks; I-DA alone is complete between dividers. 'Ida, [the Living One …]' is a contextual restoration, not a word-for-word decipherment of the damaged groups.

words.note: CONFIRMED libation formula opener. 11 attestations across 5 peak sanctuary sites. Gt-stem imperfective of √NWY.

Traces follow JA-JA on damaged surface, with no divider kept, and may belong to a following sign group; the word's length and ending are unknown. The shared beginning with PKZa18 is structurally noteworthy, and √ḥ-y-y 'live; life' remains a candidate comparison, but the fragment cannot establish /ḥayyā/ or a complete epithet.

SYZa8.coverage: 1/1 complete word translated; trailing fragment untranslated
SYZa8.notes: Context: Peak-sanctuary libation vessel (LMIA). The formula opener is followed by JA-JA-[…] at the broken right edge. Compare PKZa18, where the same preserved beginning also runs into a break; neither witness preserves a complete JA-JA word.

words.note: First sign: the foot of an upright only (DA, A, ME or SA). Fourth sign: perhaps ZU over WA over JA. Broken after SE (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 211). Not readable.

SYZb7.notes: Fragment of a terracotta zoomorphic rhyton (?) from the Syme sanctuary (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 210–11, fig. 9). Six positions, broken after the sixth. The four-sign RA-KI-NI-SE omits the fourth sign and does not support la-kinnisēt.

words.note: The signs are preserved after a broken left edge, so the inscription itself does not preserve the group's opening boundary. The recurrent formula supports segmentation as I-PI-NA-MA; the p-n 'face/front' family supports the contextual sense 'in the presence of,' and -MA may be an enclitic =ma.

A following divider secures the right boundary. 'Sacred song' renders the proposed abstract šīrūt in -ūt from √š-y-r 'sing' (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); it is not a separately written adjective and not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

VRYZa1.translation: […] in the presence of sacred song […]
VRYZa1.notes: Fragmentary witness of positions 5–6 of the IO Za 2 formula on a square serpentine libation table. The text is written retrograde. The surface is broken before I-PI-NA-MA, while a divider follows SI-RU-TE and the continuation is lost. The normalized pair is secured by intact formulaic parallels, including IO Za 2 and KO Za 1. 'Sacred song' is the English rendering adopted for the proposed abstract noun šīrūt.

words.gloss: Storm God (= Hadad/Baal)—heading/recipient; rival adû 'work assignment'

words.note: PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

HT95b.translation: For Addu: king/royal establishment 10, [break], blood (ritual category) 10, count/reckoning 10, emmer 10, nobles/council 10, parched grain 10.
HT95b.notes:
Context: Allocation ledger for the Storm God Addu—same six category words as recto (HT95a) with adjusted quantities, all standardized to 10 units except possible lost entry at break

Verso of HT95a. Same six allocation categories as recto but with different quantities—recto has SA-RU 20 and QE-RA₂-U 7; verso standardizes all to 10. The recto header DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA names the institution and commodity (grain); the verso header A-DU names the divine recipient (Storm God). Together the two sides likely represent two related distributions: one institutional (recto), one cultic (verso). The fragment markers between SA-RU and DA-ME indicate at least one lost entry. All six categories match exactly between recto and verso—the same allocation vocabulary in a different fiscal context.

words.note: Compound: SU-PU₂ /suppu/ "bowl" + *188 BUṬNU "terebinth" logogram. Commodity heading.

words.gloss: terebinth (PA₃ a phonetic complement for the b-onset)
words.note: PA₃ ba as a phonetic complement for the b of buṭnu, as *307 writes DU in *307-PU₂-RE dubur.

√q-y-n. Arabic qayn 'smith, artisan'; Sabaic qyn 'administrator, governor' (Biella 1982, 454). Also appears on HT8a recto (¾ unit)—the same recurring recipient label in both oil and terebinth registers.
√k-p-r. Here likely a recipient designation—"(for) the village."

words.gloss: He (of) Re: Egyptian personal name Pꜣ-Rꜥ (PNM v6)
words.note: Egyptian-derived PN. Receiving 1⅛ units of terebinth product.

words.gloss: terebinth product, a consignment by ship
words.note: The ship *86 joined to *188, as on ten Khania roundels: terebinth sent by sea, ½ unit. Rival: Uchitel's 'ship's load' (Uchitel 2016b, 9). See *188.

HT8b.translation: Bowl of terebinth (pistachio) nuts: 1. [divider] 5. Terebinth: 2. Qaynī (smith or administrator): 1⅜. Village: ½. Payare: 1⅛. Terebinth by ship: ½. [½].
HT8b.notes:
Context: Terebinth product accounting—commodity ledger with fractional quantities (⅜, ⅛, ½), tracking resin/mastic distributions to named recipients

Verso of HT8a. The recto records olive oil (OLE+KI) distributions; the verso records terebinth (*188) product distributions. QA-*310-I appears on both sides—the same recipient drawing from two commodity registers. Fractional quantities (⅜, ⅛, ½) suggest measurement of liquid or semi-liquid products (resin, oil). PA₃-*188 gives the b of buṭnu if PA₃ is a phonetic complement, as *307 writes DU in *307-PU₂-RE; Schrijver takes it for a transaction sign, as on HT 34 (Schrijver 2014, 7). *86+*188 is terebinth sent by ship, *86 being Uchitel's ship sign (2016b, 9). Five of six substantive words are in the lexicon (83%).

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Same formula-initial position as IOZa2.
Single sign AU followed by break. Possibly ideogram for 'pig' (SUS) per GORILA, or beginning of next formula word.

IOZa3.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—fragmentary (formula verb + damaged ending)

Fragmentary. Only the formula verb survives intact. The AU sign at the break may be ideographic (commodity) rather than part of the prayer.

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Same formula-initial position.

words.gloss: broken word after the formula verb; *321 has no value
words.note: Broken after *321 (GORILA V 28–29).

IOZa7.translation: I make myself a dwelling · JA-TI-*321[…]
IOZa7.notes: Libation table, left end intact, broken after *321 (GORILA V 28–29). The divider is cut over an erased JA.

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Syme attestation confirms inter-site formula distribution.
I-DA = Mount Ida (I-DA-A, KO Za 1; I-DA-[, IO Za 2) with the emphatic enclitic -mi, as I-PI-NA-MI-NA /ʾippina=mi=na/. Position 2 names the sanctuary's mountain, as JA-DI-KI-TU at Iouktas.
Single sign JA at break. Possibly beginning of next formula word (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME or JA-DI-KI-TU).

SYZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling—Ida herself! … [broken]
SYZa1.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—Syme variant

MMIIIB date makes this among the earliest formula attestations. I-DA-MI in position 2 names Mount Ida, with the emphatic enclitic -mi, as JA-DI-KI-TU names Dikte at Iouktas and I-DA-A Ida at Kophinas. The trailing JA- at the break hints at a continuation into the standard formula sequence.

words.note: tG-stem 1cs of √n-w-y; same reading as the other ten copies and the lexicon entry. LMIA date.

Position 2, the divine address. Vocative ya + ʾanwaru, elative of √n-w-r 'light'; I- writes the aleph. RILA-S1 p. 84 reads JA-I-NWA-RO with RO underdotted; GORILA's ZA is 'moins probable'. Sign 3 is NWA (AB48), its only occurrence in the corpus. Rival: ʾaṣwaru 'Fashioner' if AB48 wrote a sibilant + w.
Position 3. √b-n-y 'to build' — active participle with nisbe. Divine craftsman epithet (cf. Ugaritic Kothar-wa-Khasis). RILA-S1 underdots WI; PA₃-NI-PI is less plausible.

SYZa4.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Radiant One, the Builder
SYZa4.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—Syme variant with unique second and third words

LMIA Syme peak sanctuary. Word 1 is the tG-stem formula verb (CONFIRMED). Word 2 = yā ʾanwaru 'O Radiant One' (SPECULATIVE; RILA-S1 p. 84). Word 3 = bānīy 'the Builder' (CANDIDATE). The epithet pair matches Ugaritic El's ṯr il dpid // bny bnwt 'Builder of Built (Ones)' (KTU 1.4 III 30–32).

words.gloss: may you (f.) be gracious (if TA begins the word)
words.note: Conditional G u-class analysis of √n-ʿ-m. Arabic naʿuma/yanʿumu supports the u-vocalism, and Sabaic n²m ‘be favourable, prosper’ supplies the closest semantics (Beeston et al. 1982, 90). TA is the Semitic t-prefix; TI is di Mino's proposed analogical 2fs subject clitic. The initial break, unwritten ʿ, and unattested prefix verb + -tī combination keep the reading tentative; Thomas's TI-as-plural analysis remains a rival.

One graphic word across the side break. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM attests accusative /yašaram/ (Gelb 1980, no. 3448), the adverbial accusative 'in righteousness'; SA-SA writes the geminate šš, as in JA-SA-SA-RA-ME. NA is the emphatic clitic =na, as Ugaritic -n or -(Vn)na (Tropper 2000, §§89.1–2).
GORILA IV 9 prints DA-WA-[·]-ḌU-WA-ṬO, one sign lost inside the word. Not readable.
Right-broken. The preserved signs may begin the Semitic ‘island’ word, but the incomplete form cannot support the translation ‘of the island.’

KNZa10.translation: […] May you indeed be gracious and upright …
KNZa10.notes: GORILA IV, 8–9 gives ]TA-NU-MU-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-MA / NA · DA-WA-[·]-ḌU-WA-ṬO · I-JA[. No divider separates MA from NA, so JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA is one graphic word across the side break. If the initial TA begins a word, the proposed strict rendering is ‘may you be gracious—in righteousness indeed’; the smoother translation below renders the adverbial phrase as coordinated English. The lexical controls are √n-ʿ-m ‘be gracious/favourable’ and Amorite /yašaram/ ‘in righteousness’; the 2fs -tī and emphatic =na remain analogical proposals. The two final groups are damaged and left untranslated.

words.note: N-stem √ʿ-n-y in the TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU frame of IO Za 2 word 7: 2fs prefix + indicative -u + subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n. Ugaritic tʿnyn /taʿniyūna/ (KTU 1.23:12). The verb addresses and puns on the theonym that follows, I-NA-TA-I ʿInatī "my Anat".

Theonym plus 1cs -ī. I writes the ʿ, as syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ and ša-i for /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). ʿAnat is 'she who answers', √ʿ-n-y (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

words.gloss: Breast (first member of a divine epithet)
words.note: First member of ṯudī-šiqā. ZU is AB 79, ṯu, here a dotted form (Karetsou, Godart and Olivier 1985, 123); Ugaritic ṯd 'breast' (DULAT 886), also written zd and ḏd (KTU 1.23:24, 59).

words.gloss: Who Gives Drink (second member of a divine epithet)
words.note: Second member of ṯudī-šiqā; compare Ugaritic šqy, Hebrew hišqā, and Akkadian šaqû, 'give drink.' The deity-plus-epithet construction compares with Ugaritic btlt ʿnt, 'the young woman Anat' (KTU 1.3 III 11).
Adverbial accusative.

IOZa6.translation: May you answer us, my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink, in righteousness.
IOZa6.notes:
A small alabaster cup from the peak sanctuary of Mt. Iouktas, written whole in three groups, each closed by a divider. Karetsou, Godart and Olivier take it for the finest example of the libation tables' secondary formula, with PS Za 2.2 a variant. Its middle group runs eight signs without a divider; its fifth sign, a dotted AB 79 (ZU, ṯu) ringed by fifteen curved strokes, is 'non pleinement assurée', and the editors reject their first reading of it as an embellished divider (1985, 123, 137 and n. 69).

TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU is tan-ʿinā-u-tī-n(u) 'may you (f.) answer us', the frame of IO Za 2's TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU with √ʿ-n-y in the root slot: Ugaritic tʿnyn /taʿniyūna/ (KTU 1.23:12; Tropper 2000, 661), Hebrew N-stem naʿănêtî lô 'I will make answer to him' (Ezek 14:4, 7). I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA is one compound, ʿInatī ṯudī-šiqā 'my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink', the goddess and her epithet written as one word: I writes the ʿ, as syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78); ZU-DI is ṯudī, Ugaritic ṯd 'breast' (DULAT 886), also written zd and ḏd (KTU 1.23:24, 59); SI-KA is šiqā, the verbal noun of √š-q-y 'give drink', as KA-NA-SI kanāsī 'my gathering' is of √k-n-s (U-NA-KA-NA-SI); so too the name RA-NA-TU-SU rannatušu 'his shout of joy', from rannat- of √r-n-n with -šu. Cf. the compounds KA-NI-JA-MI qāniy-yammi 'Creator of the Sea', El's epithet on CR Zf 1, and DA-DU-MI-NE dādu-Mīnō 'Beloved of Minos' (KN Zf 31). 'May you answer' puns on ʿAnat, 'she who answers' (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

The Psalter has the whole line: nôrāʾôt bəṣedeq taʿănēnû ʾĕlōhê yišʿēnû 'with awesome deeds, in righteousness you answer us, Elohim of our salvation' (Ps 65:6), the verb before the vocative as in kî taʿănēnî ʾēl 'for you answer me, O El' (Ps 17:6). Ugarit nurses its king at the goddesses' breasts, ynq ḥlb aṯrt // mṣṣ ṯd btlt [ʿnt] 'who sucks the milk of Athirat, who drinks at the breast of the maiden [Anat]' (KTU 1.15 II 26–27), and Pughat gives drink to Yatpan before he answers (KTU 1.19 IV 54–56). Hanat is at Mari in Ummī-Hanat (ARM 23, 159:5), and ḫa-na-tum is Ishtar in the Amorite-Akkadian bilingual (George and Krebernik 2022, 115, 119).

words.note: The vessel is broken immediately before NA. A divider survives after SI, but no initial boundary is preserved. KH7a has the distinct form E-NA-SI and is not an independent attestation of NA-SI.
The comparison with Semitic pnm 'face, presence' is PROBABLE from five complete occurrences elsewhere. This APZa2 occurrence ends at a break without a divider and is capped at CANDIDATE.

words.gloss: a form of KU-PA₃-NA-TU, its ending lost. Not readable.
words.note: GORILA IV 5 prints ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE[, with a trace before KU, perhaps I. Neither exterior boundary nor any internal divider is preserved.

words.gloss: by the portions; rival 'by the recitation'
words.note: A divider survives after TE; the left edge is lost, and PI and MI are over an erasure (GORILA IV 5). PI the proclitic bi-, as in PI-KU-ZU; mināt 'portion', Emar mināt (GlOS 2, 45), Ug. mnt (DULAT 558). Rivals: Ug. mnt 'enumeration; spell', Heb. minḥâ 'offering'.

No divider follows TA; about three signs are lost before -QA, room for the genitive. yarēʾat, f. cs. of yārēʾ 'in fear of', Bab. yərēʾat (HALOT 433; Prov 31:30). Rivals: yārēʾtā 'you have feared' (2 Sam 1:14), the noun yirʾat (Job 28:28).
Only final QA and the following divider survive; no root or syntactic function can be recovered.

APZa2.translation: […] presence/face […] ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE-[ […] / […] by the portions; behold, she who reveres […] -QA.
APZa2.notes: Fragmentary two-line inscription on two nonjoining pieces of one serpentine jar (HM 2479 + HM 2480). Every preserved sequence is edge-damaged. I-PI-NA-MA has substantial independent lexical support. The longer sequence, ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE[ with a trace before KU (perhaps I), contains the independently attested Kupanatu base and additional morphology. The fragments do not permit reconstruction of a continuous sentence. Younger estimates six lost sign spaces in the first internal lacuna and three in the second; these are not readable signs.

words.gloss: bowl or vessel; perhaps a vessel-account heading
words.note: Compare Akkadian diqāru and Late Bronze Age Ugaritic /dikāru/ 'bowl' (alphabetic plural dkrt). Huehnergard treats the Ugaritic item as an Akkadian or shared early loan, not necessarily an inherited root. DA-QE-RA occurs on HT6a, HT57a and HT120; its written vowels do not exactly match /dikāru/.
PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

Read /Dawmi/, from √d-w-m 'endure, remain,' with U representing medial /w/ and *49 carrying /mi/. The sign may be syllabic here while functioning logographically or as an abbreviated commodity sign elsewhere; such polyvalence removes any contradiction with PALM/TREE or its candidate lexical name TAMIR.
SigLA catalogues this as the single composite logogram A517; do not segment it as I + GRA+PA without further evidence.
GORILA groups line-final KI with line-initial RE-TA-NA; the complete form is independently attested on HT2, HT8a and HT108.

HT120.translation: Vessel (DA-QE-RA) account. Blood (ritual category): grain category K+L 74 and grain category PA 62½. Dawmi: A517 20. Kretan—the Cretan or Crete: grain category B 60 and grain category PA 48. Phaistos: 3⅕.
HT120.notes: Administrative grain account arranged under parallel entity or category headings. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a ritual category heading grain allocations; its quantified use on HT95a/b and HT120 weighs against the later Aramaic dəmē 'value of', and dimtu 'district' is the other rival. DA-QE-RA has Akkadian and Ugaritic /dikāru/ 'bowl' as a Bronze Age comparison, although the written vowels differ. DA-U-*49 is read Dawmi, with *49=/mi/ here; possible logographic use of *49 elsewhere does not exclude that syllabic value. GORILA groups cross-line KI-RE-TA-NA, independently confirmed by three complete attestations. PA-I-TO securely names Phaistos. The tablet does not itself express direction, shipment or taxation.

Logographic abbreviation of terûmā (√r-w-m "to raise, lift off"). Administrative category marker: 29 standalone nodule stamps, 29 tablet occurrences in HEADING · TE · COMMODITY · NUMBER position. SAMWa1.notes:
Context: Northernmost Linear A inscription—clay nodule with libation formula vocabulary

Clay nodule sealing a shipment of 10 ¹⁄₁₆ units of unnamed commodity. Syllable sequence JA-SA SA-RA reads as JA-SA-SA-RA, the libation formula (CONFIRMED) without terminal -ME mimation. The formula on an administrative nodule labels the sealed goods as ritually consecrated. Compare IOZa12 where the same formula splits across a line break as JA-SA / SA-RA-ME. Parsing JA-SA and SA-RA as separate words (yašar 'upright' + šarra 'queen') is less economical and breaks the cross-site pattern. Northernmost Linear A inscription—Minoan ritual-administrative vocabulary extending to Samothrace.

HT87.translation: Bridegroom category; merchants: (man) of the throne-house 1; Yarīm 1; Dikise 1; Qaššāpu 1; Kurkū 1; A-RA-[…]-A-TU 1.
HT87.notes: Context: personnel register with no commodity logograms. Six entries of 1 unit follow the *21F-TU-NE and MA-KA-RI-TE rubrics. MA-KA-RI-TE is 'merchants', as on HT 117a (Ugaritic mkrm, DULAT 537); rival makritu 'red' (CAD M/1 138). PI-TA-KE-SI is bīt-kissi, a crown merchant (CAD K 593), rival Hurrian Pidi-kešḫi. Dikise is a possible Hurrian name; for the latter compare Laroche's directly attested tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful' or 'beauty' and the Amarna personal name Tagi. One entry, A-RA-[?]-A-TU, is damaged.

HT31.translation: Vessel inventory. [?]-TI-SA (unread), acquired (PU-KO): tripod cauldron (*410-VS) […]. […]5. Goblets (QA-PA₃): 10. Bowls (SU-PU): 10. Carafes (KA-RO-PA₃): 10. Set (SA-JA-MA): 30[…]. […] 10. KI-DE-MA-*323-NA[ (unread): […]. Cups (*402-VS): 400, three hundred-circles showing. Pots (SU-PA₃-RA, *402-VS): 300. Winecups (PA-TA-QE, *402-VS): 3000.
HT31.notes:
Context: Vessel inventory—the "virtual bilingual" (Stieglitz 1971). Minoan vessel names written over pictograms for each vessel type. The most important tablet for Semitic vessel-name identification.

Gordon's HT 31 vessel quartet (§163), independently confirmed by Stieglitz (Kadmos 10, 1971) and Rendsburg (Ugaritic Dictionary, forthcoming). The five names written into vessel signs all have Semitic etymologies; PU-KO pūqū 'acquired' belongs to the heading, and the tripod cauldron *410-VS, very probably of bronze (Duhoux 2002, 39), stands unnamed. Ventris & Chadwick (1956, 323): "the difference in language is obvious." Quantities suggest institutional storage: 3000, 300 and 400 of the conical *402 cup. Of the 400, three hundred-circles show; the fourth place falls in the break.

Duhoux reads the tablet as the inventory of a vessel store like Magazine 15 of the Villa, where conical cups stood stacked in the hundreds; the small conical cups are over 87% of the preserved count, as at Kea (1,164 of 1,318). Every intact number is a multiple of ten, the vessels standing in fives or tens. The 5 that opens .2 follows the break; Duhoux gives it to a lost second entry (2002, 35–36). The Linear B parallel is MY Ue 611, twelve vessel names with their counts (Duhoux 2002, 50–51). He finds su-pu plausibly Semitic and takes the vessel names, if Semitic, for loans (Duhoux 2002, 56–59).

words.note: Ug. ḥṭt 'wheat' (DULAT 372), Heb. ḥiṭṭâ (HALOT 306), -t unwritten. Heads the tablet beside VIN-SU. Also KH88, ZA14.

5-sign word, no Semitic root match. Possibly a toponym or institutional name. Receives 6 units.
√s-m-d. Akk. samīdu 'groats, coarse meal' (temple ration lists). Also ZA15a. -E suffix may be Minoan grammatical ending.

ZA5a.notes:
Context: Ration list: wheat and wine distributed to priests and a named recipient

Ration tablet from Zakros. Wheat (ḥiṭṭa) and wine head the tablet, then priests (7 units) and an opaque recipient (6 units), followed by semolina. Commodity pattern (wine + grain + priestly recipients) parallels HT89, HT95a/b.

√ʾ-r-ṣ̂. PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂- 'earth' (SRJ #768). Emphatic lateral ṣ̂ dropped. Feminine noun. Co-occurs with A-RE-TU-MI on same tablet—same root, different morphology. 4 units.
NWS compound: √ʾ-r-ṣ̂ 'earth' + √ʾ-m-m 'mother' + 1cs possessive -ī. Same ṣ̂-loss as A-RA-TU. Proposed Semitic etymology of Greek Artemis. Tablet breaks after this word—quantity or further text lost.

ZA7a.notes:
Context: Votive offering allocation: burnt and earth offerings dedicated under the earth-goddess epithet. Tablet broken after A-RE-TU-MI—original text longer.

Incomplete—tablet broken after A-RE-TU-MI (damage marker). Zakros tablet with votive allocations. All three words share a chthonic/earth-offering semantic field: burnt offering (ʿūlū), earth (ʾarṣ̂atu), and the earth-goddess epithet (ʾarṣ̂-ummī = pre-Greek Artemis). The A-RA-TU / A-RE-TU-MI co-occurrence strengthens both readings—same √ʾ-r-ṣ̂ root in bare noun and compound PN on a single tablet.

words.note: TE functions as an administrative category or transaction marker in 56 documents: commodity-number entries and isolated nodules establish the function. Hebrew tə-rûmā (Exod 25:2) and Ugaritic trmt 'offering' (KTU 1.43:3; 1.6 VI:44) support 'contribution/offering,' but the single sign does not spell the full word; terûmā remains a proposed logographic value.

A-DU occurs in 10 documents at three sites, regularly as an administrative heading. The spelling fits the Old Babylonian Amorite/Akkadian divine name Addu; alternatively, Akkadian adû means 'a (day's) work, stint.' The sequence may be homographic across different administrative contexts. Its position between TE and the commodities here slightly favors a named recipient such as Addu, but does not confirm the divine interpretation.
GRA is the grain commodity logogram; the tablet records 680 units. The proposed spoken label dagān is not required for the translation.

words.gloss: oil/fat-register commodity; perhaps fat or tallow: 12
words.note: A non-phonetic commodity ideogram occurring 42 times on 38 tablets, commonly beside GRA, OLE, OLIV, and related commodities. Its distribution permits an oil/fat product; Hebrew peder 'suet' supplies a semantic comparison, not a demonstrated spoken value. It is distinct from OLE and must not be translated 'olive oil.'

HT92.notes: Context: Administrative allocation from Casa Room 7, Haghia Triada, LM IB; HT Scribe 2. The tablet is substantially intact and no written group is cut by an edge. SigLA records an erased GRA sign, which is not part of the surviving transliteration. TE marks the transaction or category; A-DU may name Addu or an administrative work-stint. GRA is secure, whereas *304 remains an unidentified oil/fat-register commodity. No particular measurement units can be inferred from the 680:12 ratio.

Numeral.
Egyptian ḏd-kꜣ + -s 'her', the pattern of Djedkare (Ḏd-kꜣ-Rꜥ); DI-DI writes ḏd, as on DI-DI-ZA-KE (HT 1) and DI-DI-KO-RA-ME-TA₂ (ZA 11a). Rival: Semitic dādī-kussē 'my beloved is the throne'.
Phoenician healing deity. √ʾ-š-m-n. SA writes /š/ (sibilant merger). Dative: 'to Eshmun.' Rival: Woudhuizen (2016, 229–230) reads Akkadian assammû 'a large drinking vessel' (CAD A/2 339–340).

ʾāsē 'physician': Akk. asû, Aram. ʔsy(ʔ), Arb. ʔāsin (GlOS 1, 47). The title follows the healing god's name, as A-KO-A-NE follows PI-TE-RI. Four attestations (HT81, HT93a, HT132, ZAZb3). Rival: ʾaššē 'fire offering'.

ZA Zb 3 .2, the formula's A-TA-I-*301- frame with -DE-KA. A- is the 1cs prefix, -TA- the t-stem, I-*301 (*301 = na) the root √ʿ-n-w 'to be humbled', its ʿ unwritten, and -DE-KA dēka 'for you', the relative dē + 2ms -ka (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Hebrew keeps this t-stem, hitʿannâ 'to submit' (Gen 16:9) and 'to bow humbly' before God (Dan 10:12, Ezra 8:21; HALOT 852–54); Ugaritic ʿnw 'to be humbled' (DULAT 168–69), Arabic ʿanati l-wujūhu 'faces are humbled' (Q 20:111). Rival: √ʿ-n-y 'to answer', the root of TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU, 'I answer for you'; it has no t-stem in Hebrew or Ugaritic (HALOT 851–52; DULAT 169).

Vocative ʾa- + rāpiʾ 'healer' (√r-p-ʾ) + rinnā 'joyful cry' (√r-n-n), naming the god -DE-KA addresses, as rōpʾekā 'your healer' (Exod 15:26); the healer's title fits A-SA-MU-NE Eshmun, the healing god, on the same inscription. RE-PI is written over an erased PI (GORILA IV 113). Rival: Gordon's re-ma-re-na, mārēnā 'our lord', with MA for PI.

√n-t-k 'pour out' (Ugaritic tntkn, KTU 1.14 I 28–30; Akkadian natāku), the nun assimilated to geminate tt and written TI-TI. Header of HT35, a list of pourable goods; here the last word of the wine libation. Rival: a toponym Tittiku.

ZAZb3.translation: Wine, 32. Djed-ka(.s) to Eshmun the Physician: I humble myself for you, O Healer of Jubilation. May it be poured out.
ZAZb3.notes:
Context: LMIB dedicatory inscription on a clay pithos. Contains libation formula in Zakros dialect (-DE-KA variant) + Egyptian theophoric personal name + libation verb.

Dedicatory inscription: commodity (VIN 32) + dedicant (Egyptian PN) + deity (Eshmun) + title (ʾāsē 'physician') + Zakros libation formula √ʿ-n-w + Eshmun epithet (compound √r-p-ʾ + √r-n-n) + closing TI-TI-KU 'may it be poured' (√n-t-k). The -DE-KA libation variant is unique to Zakros, establishing a 5th dialectal form. A-RE-PI-RE-NA is a compound divine epithet rather than a hapax PN, given its thematic convergence with Eshmun and the rpʾ/rnn liturgical dyad (Psalm 30:3-6). The 32 units, some 921.6 litres, would fill six pithoi of this size, the number found in magazine Θ; for Schoep and Driessen the text refers to more than this jar's contents, perhaps to an occasion over the batch of pithoi (2003, 79).

words.meaning: O ʾAyaku (personal name, 'Where are you?'), vocative

KNZf13.translation: Coffin of Sidon. Weeping in the house. My head you lift up, O ʾAyaku.
KNZf13.notes: Gold ring HM 530, from compartment E of Chamber Tomb IX at Mavro Spilio, the compartment of a larnax; the silver pin KN Zf 31 comes from the same tomb (Olivier 1982). 19 signs in a spiral from the outer band inward, no dividers; RI (12, 15), MU (16) and KU (19) dotted (GORILA IV 152–153). The corpus sets the boundaries (SI-DI-, -DI-NA, PA-JA-, TE-RI, A-JA-KU), Olivier's frequency division with two groups split. A lament: the coffin, the weeping in the house, and the Psalm idiom 'you lift up my head' (Ps 3:4) addressed to ʾAyaku. Kirta's death-lament gathers the same words: bt 'house', bky 'weep', rỉš 'head' and ỉk 'how?' (KTU 1.16 I 2–28). Tabnit of Sidon pairs ʾrn and ṣdnm on his coffin (KAI 13). Rival for signs 12–16: SE-TE-RI-MU sitrum 'protection'; Ps 27:4–6 has the words of both readings, bêt YHWH, sēter and yārûm rōʾšî, in three verses.

KNZf31.translation: ]SI[ ]SI-ZA-NE-*310, Dādu-Mīnō, 'Beloved of Minos', who stands, he is fire, ʾAwpiʿ, 'he shone forth': she serves; give him drink! The pin: fix it, you have fastened it. She will remember, by that with which one curls the hair.
KNZf31.notes: Longest multi-word metal inscription in the Linear A corpus. 8 of 9 words are hapax legomena. Eight words are read, all SPECULATIVE; ]SI-ZA-NE-*310 is broken and unread. GORILA IV 155 prints two lines; ]SI[ stands apart before the first. The first line names the man, DA-DU-MI-NE, QA-MI-*47-NA-RA and A-WA-PI being name shapes at Ebla, Mari and Ugarit; 'who stands: He is fire' and 'he shone forth' are the theophany's words (Ps 68:2; 50:2–3). It closes with the woman's charge to serve him. The second line opens with A-DA-RA, the pin naming itself, and speaks to its wearer: she fastens it, and remembers him by it when she curls her hair. A man's gift of a silver hair pin to a woman, a row of crocus blossoms on the reverse. Three of its verbs, √s-ʔ-d, √š-q-y and √ḫ-s-s, meet in one Ugaritic scene: Kothar-wa-Ḫasis brings the bow, and Danatiya gives him drink and serves him (KTU 1.17 V 19–31). The opening is corroded, about three signs lost between ]SI[ and ]SI-ZA-NE-*310 (GORILA IV 154): the likeliest place for the woman's name, the subject of both 'she' verbs. The tail ZA-NE-*310 may be zānin 'provider', Akkadian zāninu, the king who feeds a temple (CAD Z 43, 45; √z-w-n, Heb. māzôn), *310 writing -in as in KI-*310-RE kinnāre: the man's first title, answered by 'she serves; give him drink'. SI would then end a word joined to it, as TE-SU-DE-SE-KE-I joins two. Rival: *310 as ni, a Hurrian name in -zanni, -zinni (Izzanni, ARM XVI/1 133; Izzinni, PIHANS 117, 132).

The likely formulaic restoration A-SA-SA-RA-[ME] is supported by complete A-SA-SA-RA-ME at IO Zb 10 and recurrent JA-SA-SA-RA-ME. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM (Gelb 1980, no. 3448) supports √y-š-r with accusative -am. KNZc6.translation: My incense: until fine, flask. NI-JA-NU. JU-KU-NA-PA-KU-NU-U-[?]-I-ZU.
KNZc6.notes: Ink-written clay cup (HM 2630), pair of KN Zc 7, from an upper MM III floor above the Basement of the Monolithic Pillars, Knossos, the crypt of a sanctuary (Evans, PoM I 587–588, 613–616). Three circular registers read as a spiral from the bottom. Register .1 QI-TI-RI heads the text, register .2 gives the incense as ground fine (A-DI DA-KI-TI, Hebrew qəṭōret … daqqâ, Lev 16:12) and the flask (PA-KU). NI-JA-NU is unread. Register .3, one group with a sign lost, is unread. Word division follows Evans (PoM I 615 n. 1), who reports dividing marks before A, DA and NI; GORILA IV 121 prints only the last. Younger reads A-DI-DA-KI-TI-PA-KU as a muddled A-DI-KI-TE. Marinatos set the two cups beside the inverted bowls of Nippur, inked with Aramaic incantations against evil spirits (Marinatos 1951, 41); Franceschetti adds the spiral script those bowls share and the Keftiu spells of the London Medical Papyrus (Franceschetti 1990, 40–41).

words.note: Group-writing: s3bw [first half of element 6]. √s-b-b 'to turn, go around' — 2mp imperative *sabbū addressing disease demons (plural). Heb sābab (~163 occ., HALOT 738), 2mp imper. sōbbū (Ps 48:13 סֹבּוּ צִיּוֹן 'Go round Zion'). The s in s3bw is plain /s/, not /ṣ/: the same scribe renders Semitic ṣ as Egyptian ḏ in the adjacent word yaṣʾā (y3yd33). Geminate -bb- invisible in group-writing (standard). D54 determinative is embedded in the phonogram ḏi of word 2 (Kyriakidis 2002, n. 16), not a freestanding classifier per word. Disease-expulsion doublet sabbū yaṣʾā 'Turn away! Go out!' parallels Akkadian serial motion imperatives in Udug.hul. Akulov reads the entire element as one word sa-bu-ja-ja-dza with root reduplication (Hattic analysis); our NWS parse splits it into two standard Semitic motion verbs. The sibilant correspondence excludes √ṣ-b-ʾ.

Group-writing: y3yd33 [second half of element 6, Det: 'to go' (D54)]. √y-ṣ-ʾ 'to go out' — 3ms volitive yaqtula (Moran 1960), 'may it go out!' PS *wṣʾ: Akk waṣû 'to go out' (CAD W 319, preserves original *w-), Ug yṣʾ (DLU 946), Heb yāṣāʾ (HALOT 427), Aram yṣʾ. The initial *w→y shift is a diagnostic NWS sound change. Egyptian d renders Semitic ṣ (no native ṣ); 33 (double ayin) renders final ʾ + ā vowel. STEINER'S OWN ROOT: Steiner 1992 identifies √y-ṣ-ʾ yaṣʾā 'go out!' in this spell — not our proposal alone.

Group-writing: hwnm'k3tw [element 7, Det: A2 'to speak/think']. √ḥ-n-q 'to strangle, throttle' — feminine personification *ḥanqatu 'she who strangles,' a disease-demon name. Pan-Semitic: Akk ḫanāqu 'to strangle' (CAD Ḫ 75), Heb ḥānaq (Nahum 2:13), Syr ḥnaq, Ar ḫanaqa. Egyptian h for Semitic ḥ is standard in group-writing. The m' in the middle is problematic — Steiner reads through it (possibly a vowel marker or scribal convention). STEINER'S READING: Steiner 1992 reads ḥ-m-k-tu = ḥanqatu 'strangulation demon.' The samānu disease involves swelling and constriction, making a 'strangler-demon' etiology medically coherent.

Group-writing: rp33y [element 8, Det: A40 'seated god' (male)]. √r-p-ʾ 'to heal' + 1cs possessive -ī = 'my healer.' Pan-Semitic: Ug rpʾu divine title (KTU 1.108:1 rpʾu mlk ʿlm 'the Healer, eternal king'; KTU 1.20–22 rpʾīm/Rephaim ancestral healer-spirits), Heb rāpāʾ (Exod 15:26 kī ʾanī YHWH rōpʾekā 'for I am YHWH your healer'; Ps 103:3 hā-rōpēʾ ləkol-taḥăluʾāyəkī 'who heals all your diseases'), Phoen mrpʾ month name (KAI 37:3, 'healing month'), Aram rpʾ. The A40 determinative confirms divine status. STEINER'S READING: Steiner 1992 reads r-p-y = rpʾy 'my Healer.' A Keftiu deity Rpʾī invoked against disease is semantically transparent and parallels the Ugaritic Rapʾu cult. Akulov reads Erupa-j and connects to Greek Europa via Hattic *lup 'bull' — our reading and his share the same consonantal skeleton but diverge on etymology.

Group-writing: p33wry [element 9, Det: A2 'to speak/think']. √p-ʿ-r 'to open wide (the mouth)' + 1cs suffix -ī = 'my opening (of the mouth),' i.e. 'my cry / my invocation.' Heb pāʿar 'to open wide' (Isa 5:14 ūpāʿărāh pīhā 'and opened wide its mouth'; Ps 119:131 pī pāʿartī 'I opened my mouth wide'), Ar faġara 'to open the mouth' (with regular ʿ→ġ). The A2 'to speak' determinative fits an oral invocation verb. Form *paʿūr-ī: verbal noun (qatūl pattern) + possessive = 'my crying out.' Alternative: √p-ʾ-r 'to glorify' (Heb pāʾar, Isa 60:7) — 'my glorification,' less compelling with speech determinative. Structurally sits between the two deity names (rpʾī and Mayyā), functioning as the invocation bridge: 'My Healer — I cry out to — Mayyā.'

Group-writing: m'y3 [element 10, Det: A40 'seated god' (male)]. Deity name — deified Water. √m-y-y 'water': Heb mayim (dual form, base *may-/*mayy-), Ug my, Akk mû, Ar māʾ. A deity *Mayyā 'Water' invoked alongside *Rpʾī 'my Healer' in a disease spell: the Healer cures, the Water purifies. The Egyptian instructions prescribe reciting the spell 'over liquid, fermented drink, urine' — all water-based media, because the spell invokes the water deity. The A40 determinative marks male gender — either the Egyptian scribe's default for foreign deities, or Mayyā was male in Keftiu religion and later feminized as Greek Μαῖα (Maia, Pleiad, mother of Hermes). Akulov connects to Pleiades' heliacal rising (navigation season marker). Alternative: substrate theonym without transparent Semitic etymology.

LMP-Spell33.translation: Turn away! Go out, strangling-demon! My Healer — I cry out to Mayyā!
LMP-Spell33.notes:
Context: Keftiu medical incantation against samānu disease (mycetoma/ergotism). London Medical Papyrus lines ~11,8–12. Recorded in Egyptian group-writing (syllabic orthography), not Linear A script. Six Keftiu words (five written elements, one containing two words) with Egyptian determinatives marking word boundaries and grammatical classes. Copied late 18th Dynasty, 14th century BCE (Steiner 1992, n. 5). The spell is preceded by the Egyptian frame: 'A spell about samānu illness [that] spreads through grain and soil:' and followed by the instruction 'this spell to be said 4 times.' Cf. Steiner 1992 (JNES 51) who reads spells #27–31 and #33 as NWS but skips #32 as 'non-Semitic.' Akulov 2023 provides the most detailed modern transliteration; Akulov reads through Hattic, we read through NWS.

EXTERNAL SOURCE: Not Linear A script. Keftiu language recorded in Egyptian group-writing (syllabic orthography) in the London Medical Papyrus (BM 10059), 14th century BCE. STRUCTURE: Double imperative (disease expulsion) + vocative demon name + deity invocation + invocation verb + deity invocation. Classic ANE incantation formula: (1) command disease to depart, (2) name the demon (= power over it), (3) invoke protective deities. STEINER 1992 CONTEXT: Steiner (JNES 51) reads all surrounding spells (#27–31, #33) as NWS (Phoenician-Aramaic mix) but explicitly skips #32 as 'non-Semitic.' DEITY PAIRING: rpʾī (Healer) + Mayyā (Water) = cure + purification. The Ugaritic Rapʾu cult (KTU 1.108) and the water-based ritual instructions ('recite over liquid') confirm both elements. Sources: Akulov 2017/2023 (transliteration, Hattic reading), Steiner 1992 (NWS partial reading), Kyriakidis 2002 (phonological analysis), Wreszinski 1912 (editio princeps), Haider 2001 (initial identification of Keftiu deities).

PH6.translation: The dwelling of the Mount of She-of-the-Bull—of Mount Ida—in righteousness.
PH6.notes:
Context: MM IIB clay tablet (3 × 5.4 cm) from the Phaistos palace—among the oldest Linear A tablets, and the only numeral-free multi-word syllabic text in the untranslated residue. A proto-libation-formula dedication: both thematic roots of the LM I peak-sanctuary formula (√n-w-y 'dwelling', √y-š-r 'righteousness') appear here roughly three centuries before the stone vessels. The heading spells nawā phonetically with plain NA, predating the *301 rebus convention (*301 = /na/ derives from this root). Kamares cave sanctuary, on Ida's south face overlooking Phaistos, peaks in use MM IB–IIB—the tablet's own generation.

A-RI is read harrī 'mountain of', over ʿalē 'upon, for' (the house dative is la-, and the A-RA/A-RI/A-RU case triple argues nominal inflection) and ʾarī 'lion' (circular with the A-RI-NI-TA derivation). Alternate rendering under ʿalē: 'A dwelling—for She-of-the-Bull, for Ida—in righteousness.' Open caveat: ṯawrīnīt-a keeps -TA where the construct chain expects genitive -TI; the gentilic family shows both surface forms (-TA HT25a/ZA8, -TI KHWc2005 kanaʿanītī), so divine names may stand diptotic/frozen. No word parses as a verb: the text is a nominal dedication throughout.
